result: Systematic review: CFS patients do less daily physical activity and have lower peak isometric strength than sedentary controls, and the weighted evidence, though conflicting, points to reduced physiological exercise capacity.
reason: Review of exercise capacity vs sedentary controls supports reduced peak capacity; no numbers in abstract

result: Systematic review concludes peak isometric muscle strength is lower in CFS than in healthy sedentary controls.
reason: Supports only the lower-strength part; repeated-grip fatigability and recovery were not assessed, so not a replication

result: In 44 adolescents with CFS vs 52 controls, 24-h ambulatory recording showed significantly higher night-time heart rate, mean arterial and diastolic blood pressure.
reason: Elevated HR matches the resting-HR part, but in adolescents during sleep with BP and no HRV measure; extends rather than replicates

result: In 44 adolescents with CFS vs 52 controls, night-time heart rate and blood pressure were higher on 24-h ambulatory monitoring.
reason: Measures cardiovascular values during sleep, not sleep latency, WASO, efficiency or PSG; already covered by the neuro-hrv link

result: Over 4 years in 74 Fukuda CFS patients, fatigue (FIS) improved in 39% (by >=10 points in 26%) and worsened by >=10 points in 45%; current fatigue was independently predicted by baseline fatigue, depression, orthostatic symptoms and change in anxiety.
reason: Adult clinic cohort long-term course, consistent with low recovery and ~39% improvement; adds orthostatic association

result: Systematic review of 17 studies: 14 found lower physical activity in CFS; meta-analysis of 7 studies put daily activity at 68% of controls, with no significant difference in variability (CV 34.3% vs 31.5%).
reason: Shows lower activity levels but does not test whether deconditioning explains exercise or muscle abnormalities; no atlas finding on activity levels

result: In 25 children with CFS/ME vs 23 controls, isoprostanes were higher (252.3 vs 215.6 pg/mL, P=.007) and vitamin C lower (0.84 vs 1.15 mg/dL), with more white-cell apoptosis and normal arterial stiffness.
reason: Oxidative stress shown with different markers (isoprostanes, vitamin C) in a paediatric cohort; extends, not a same-measure replication

result: Arterial wave reflection (systemic arterial stiffness) was within the reference range in 25 children with CFS/ME vs 23 controls.
reason: Measures arterial stiffness by wave reflection, not FMD or PORH; no atlas finding on arterial stiffness

result: Of 54 adolescents with CFS followed a mean 2.2 years, 51.9% had nearly complete symptom improvement and 48.1% did not; older age at inclusion was a risk factor for non-recovery.
reason: Adolescent cohort, not adult; supports the better adolescent prognosis noted in the detail, so extends rather than replicates

result: In 246 prospectively followed glandular fever patients, 9.4% had chronic fatigue at 3 months and 7.8% CFS at 6 months; anxiety, depression, somatisation, perfectionism, negative illness beliefs and all-or-nothing behaviour (strongest) predicted CFS.
reason: Finds psychological/behavioural predictors, contradicting the claim that psychological factors do not predict post-infective fatigue; acute severity not assessed
